title: Chaining Skills to Hijack LLM Agents
abstract: arXiv:2610.01564v1 Announce Type: cross  Abstract: LLM agents use skills to improve performance on specialized tasks. To complete a user request, an agent may invoke several skills in sequence, allowing information produced under one skill to guide the next. Because skills may come from open-source repositories, this handoff can also carry attacker-controlled claims into later decisions. In this paper, we introduce APEX, which constructs and refines adversarial skill chains tailored to a user task and an attacker-selected action. The key insight is that an agent-written record of genuine task progress can carry a false claim of user approval across skills: an upstream skill induces the agent to create the record, and a downstream skill uses it to direct the attacker-selected action. Across four targeted-action families and six models on SkillsBench, the chains induce the selected action in 512 of 690 attempts (74.2%). translated_title: 串联技能以劫持大语言模型智能体
translated_abstract: LLM智能体使用技能来提升在专门任务上的表现。为了完成用户请求，智能体可能按顺序调用多个技能，使一个技能产生的信息能够指导下一个技能。由于技能可能来自开源仓库，这种交接过程也可能将攻击者控制的声明带入后续决策中。本文提出了APEX，该方法针对特定用户任务和攻击者选定的动作来构建并优化对抗性技能链。其核心洞察是：智能体自写的真实任务进度记录可以在技能之间携带虚假的用户批准声明——上游技能诱导智能体创建该记录，下游技能则利用它来引导智能体执行攻击者选定的动作。在SkillsBench上针对四个目标动作类别和六个模型的实验中，这些技能链在690次尝试中的512次（74.2%）成功诱导了选定动作。在GPT-5.4上，完整技能链在84.3%的尝试中成功。
tldr: 该论文提出APEX对抗性攻击框架，利用智能体自写的任务进度记录在技能链中夹带虚假的用户批准声明，从而劫持LLM智能体执行攻击者选定的恶意动作，在六个模型上平均攻击成功率达74.2%。
en_tdlr: The paper introduces APEX, an adversarial attack framework that hijacks LLM agents by carrying false user-approval claims across chained skills through agent-written task progress records, achieving a 74.2% success rate in inducing attacker-selected actions across six models.
